topic: ECB data: 44% of eurozone workers use AI weekly at work; for users with no productivity gain, checking and fixing AI output is the top reason
approved_script:
Nearly half of workers in the eurozone now use AI every week. But not all of them are getting more done.

That's new data from the European Central Bank, released Friday.

In August, 44 percent of working people there said they used AI at work weekly. About 18 percent used it daily.

Around 56 percent of users said it helps them get more done.

But for those who saw no gain, the top reason was the time spent checking and fixing the AI's work.

The real skill isn't using AI. It's knowing when to trust it.

recording_directions.opening_expression: Open with a slight nod and raised eyebrows on 'every week', then a knowing half-smile on 'not all of them'.
pauses: before 'But for those who saw no gain'
pronunciation: European Central Bank: say it in full
recording_directions.framing: Vertical 9:16, chest-up medium close-up, eyes on the upper third; leave headroom for on-screen numbers; plain background.
recording_directions.pace: Natural and clear (about 140 words per minute); slow slightly on the 'checking and fixing' line.
recording_directions.gestures: Open palm on 'nearly half'; small shrug on 'not all of them'; tap the desk or mime typing on 'checking and fixing'; point to camera on 'when to trust it'.

audio: Denoise and de-reverb dialogue, gentle compression, normalise to -14 LUFS with -1.5 dB true peak; tighten pauses over 0.45 s without clipping words
captions_style: Word-level burned-in captions from captions.txt, 2-5 words per line; highlight the numbers and 'checking and fixing'; keep clear of the bottom UI area
notes: Do not use unrelated stock footage or invent product demos; credit the ECB on screen for screenshots and data.
